title: Development of Mass Spectrometry Strategies to Decipher Dynamic Lysosomal Dysfunctions in Frontotemporal Dementia
text:
Frontotemporal dementia is the most common form of dementia for people under age 60, but curative
treatment is currently unavailable due to our limited understanding of the molecular etiology. This proposed
research aims at developing mass spectrometry-based strategies to determine how GRN mutations, which
result in progranulin deficiency, impair lysosomal functions and eventually lead to frontotemporal dementia.
The molecular insights gained from this research will decipher the relationship between progranulin,
lysosomes, and frontotemporal dementia, providing potential therapeutic target to develop disease-
modifying treatments for FTD.

title: Investigating the mechanism of corneal lens development
text:
The human cornea is a curved structure that focuses light onto the retina, and abnormalities in corneal
curvature lead to visual disorders like myopia, hyperopia, astigmatism and keratoconus. Using a simple model
system, the fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster, I will investigate how the shape of the corneal lens, structure similar
to human cornea, is controlled by the cells that secrete it. I will also establish the Drosophila corneal lens as a
model to study and develop treatments for glaucoma.

title: Dynamic Predictors of Sudden Cardiac Death
text:
We will assess whether the combination of static and dynamic risk will improve the risk prediction of sudden
cardiac death. We propose to use both conventional and deep learning methods to achieve this goal.

title: Deep learning to assess the role of early renal fibrosis on cardiac remodeling
text:
More than 8 in 10 Americans suffer from Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic (CKM) Syndrome, a disorder where
fibrosis is a central feature affecting the heart and kidney, which will cost the United States over $500 billion
annually. The goal of this work is to broadly understand how early-stage kidney fibrosis relates to heart disease
by leveraging deep-learning tools to process large-scale imaging data, genetic sequencing, and health record
data. This understanding could promote development of novel therapeutics to reduce heart disease risk, which
represents an urgent unmet societal need.

title: Modulating the Stem Cell Niche Set Point to Improve Skeletal Muscle Regeneration
text:
Skeletal muscle is central to everything we do and must repair to meet the vital demands of
human life. Human pluripotent stem cells are the only in vitro system that can create unlimited
numbers of muscle cells in a dish. How hPSCs commit to all stages of skeletal muscle growth
and how to support these muscle cells once they are created is pivotal to improve our
understanding of skeletal muscle repair, development, and to design better cell therapies.
Skeletal muscle stem cells are supported by their niche, but the molecular cues regulating the
niche of hPSC muscle cells has only begun to be explored. This proposal seeks to regulate the
hPSC muscle niche to better support the number and function of muscle cells created by
hPSCs.

title: Evaluating METTL1-mediated m7G tRNA methylation as a novel dependency in alveolar rhadomyosarcoma
text:
Alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma (ARMS) is the most common childhood sarcoma and is driven by the
PAX3/7-FOXO1 fusion protein. Therapeutically targeting the PAX3/7-FOXO1 fusion protein has proven
challenging and there remains a critical need to identify new novel dependencies and targets that may prove
as more effective therapeutic avenues. The K00 phase of this proposal will profile the METTL1-dependent
changes in m7G tRNA methylation and establish METTL1 and/or its targets as potential therapeutic targets for
the treatment of ARMS.

title: Targeting checkpoint inhibitors for pain control
text:
Targeting the immune checkpoint inhibitory proteins, such as programmed cell death protein-1 ligand 1 (PD-L1)
and its receptor PD-1 has saved many lives of cancer patients. The overall goal of this application is to investigate
and validate how the PD-L1/PD-1 immune checkpoint cascade controls physiological and pathological pain and
opioid analgesia via neuronal, immune, and glial regulations. Successful completion of this project will provide
novel insights into distinct actions of checkpoint pathway activators and inhibitors for the management of different
types of pain.

title: SRIN009, a cannabidiol formulation to treat chemotherapy-induced neuropathic pain
text:
Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) is a debilitating adverse effect that can lead to early
cessation of cancer treatment, resulting in an increased risk of recurrence and decreased survival rate. As there
are currently no FDA-approved treatments for CIPN, our laboratory was the first to describe the protective effects
of the non-psychoactive cannabinoid cannabidiol (CBD) in rodent models of CIPN. To improve CBD's safety and
efficacy, we will determine the safety and effectiveness of more bioavailable nanoemulsion formulations of CBD
versus traditional CBD formulation, as well as determine the potential interactive effects of this formulation with
the anti-neoplastic effects of select cancer treatments.

title: Determining the Role of Replication Protein A in Polymerase Theta-Mediated End-Joining
text:
This project will determine the role of the eukaryotic single-strand DNA binding protein RPA in regulating
polymerase theta-mediated end-joining, a mutagenic repair pathway that is upregulated in many cancer cells.
Understanding the molecular mechanism of this pathway will allow us to better target it in cancer therapies.

title: EvoCell: Using cell evolution in nematodes to model, predict, and controlcell identity in animals
text:
The bodies of humans and other animals are built from many different types of cells, but we are only beginning
to understand how genes determine these cell types or evolve to form new cell types. An understanding of
mechanisms controlling cell identity is essential to solve biomedical challenges from precision medicine to the
development of improved tissues and organs for medicine and biotechnology. Using five evolutionarily distinct
nematode worms as an experimental system, we will develop and test a computational model to predict how
animal cell types are determined.

title: Pharmacogenomics Workflow: Identifying Biomarkers and Treatment Options
text:
We will build a clinical workflow product to integrate the pharmacogenetic analysis of sequencing data into
routine clinical workflows, supporting compliance with prescribing guidance from the Food and Drug
Administration, and recommendations from the American College of Medical Genetics, Association of
Molecular Pathology, while reducing the cost and turn around time.

title: DYRK1A inhibitors, GLP1 Receptor Agonists and Immunomodulation for Beta Cell Regeneration Therapy in Type 1 Diabetes
text:
Type 1 diabetes (T1D) affects ~2 million people in the U.S. and represents a major burden to society in terms of
health costs, loss of productivity, as well as reduced life expectancy and loss of life due to acute and chronic
complications. Only a small percentage of youth (17%) and adults (21%) achieve optimal glycemic control with
exogenous insulin replacement therapy, therefore federal agencies and T1D foundations have recognized that
insulin is not a cure and identified a clear need to cure diabetes. This study will advance a novel combination
therapy with immunomodulators (anti-CD3 and/or IL-2), novel and safer DYRK1A inhibitors and clinically used
GLP1RAs to control islet autoimmunity, expand beta cell mass, and support beta cell function for T1D reversal.

title: Elucidating the Role of the Vaginal Microbiome and Daily Stress in Precancerous Cervical Lesions: A Multi-level Study.
text: This career development award proposes a multi-omic systems biology approach to elucidate how the vaginal microbiome and psychological stress contribute to the progression of precancerous cervical lesions to cancer. The proposed plan will accelerate this early-stage investigator’s career trajectory to independence by providing targeted bioinformatic, statistical and molecular biology training to analyze microbiome and stress experience data, using an integrative systems biology framework to inform future clinically relevant prognostic biomarkers, risk stratification protocols, and interventions to intercept cervical cancer development.

title: Workshop on Statistical Genetic Methods for Human Complex Traits
text:
This research education meets the need for training in methods of statistical genetics for mental health
researchers working with genome wide association studies, next generation sequencing studies, and twin and
family studies of genetic and environmental influences on mental illnesses. The introduction of new techniques
of statistical and computational genetics, and the increasing interest in the methodology for identifying the
genes influencing complex traits, has created an enormous demand for this training.

title: Tumor-associated pDC (TApDC) in liver cancer with HIV infection
text:
The goals are to study functions of tumor-associated plasmacytoid dendritic cells (TApDC) in human liver cancer
during HIV infection and immunotherapy, and to develop novel therapeutics to treat liver cancer in HIV-infected
patients. Key findings will be confirmed in future clinical studies, including clinical trials, in liver cancer patients
with and without HIV infection.

title: Dynamic imaging of lung function in free-breathing subjects
text:
In this project, we propose to develop a technique to dynamically image the lung using 129Xe MRI during free-
breathing; in addition to enabling a more physiologically accurate assessment of lung function compared to
current imaging techniques performed during breath-hold, this method will be feasible in patient populations that
have thus far been inaccessible to functional lung imaging with polarized gas due to poor breath-hold tolerance,
such as young children, those with end-stage lung disease, etc. Finally, we will establish the repeatability and
sensitivity of this technique in both healthy subjects and at-risk smokers / early COPD patients.

title: UC Davis Training Program in Chemical Biology
text: The UC Davis T32 Training Program in Chemical Biology (CPB T32) will provide pre-doctoral cross-training at the chemistry/biology interface to prepare students for impactful careers in the biomedical workforce to address societal needs in human health. The program will use evidence-based training methods to nurture productive, rigorous and resilient scientists and effective cross-disciplinary communicators.

title: Programmable nucleic acid cytometry for unraveling heterogeneity in tumors and therapies
text:
The emergence and persistence of cancer cells are intimately tied to changes in nucleic acids, including the
acquisition of somatic mutations. However, limited technologies enable separating, quantifying, and profiling
specific populations defined by nucleic acid features. Here, we will enhance emerging technologies to sort and
profile cells based on heterogeneous nucleic acids, enabling a rational, fully programmable toolkit to study cells
in cancer-associated settings, including tumor evolution and cell therapies.

title: Biogenesis of mRNA-derived telomerase long noncoding RNA
text:
RNA molecules are vital to many cellular functions in biology. Telomerase RNA is a class of long noncoding RNA
(lncRNA) that plays an essential role in telomerase function, telomere maintenance, and chromosome stability.
This research program aims to understand an unprecedented mRNA-derived biogenesis pathway of telomerase
RNA in a fungal model organism, which will provide unforeseen insights into how mRNA may be processed to
generate lncRNA and have broad impacts on RNA biology and human diseases.

title: Development of PRECISE: A Data Driven Personalized Suicide Prevention Intervention
text:
Suicide is a leading cause of death in the United States. Individuals at high-risk of suicide are a heterogeneous
population. Building from an emerging line of evidence showing the effectiveness of personalized treatments for
mental health problems, we plan to refine and test a personalized intervention for reducing suicidal thoughts and
behaviors.
